subject: Urgent: Core inference queueing impact — exec attention requested
messages:
From: Thomas Li <thomas.li@clearpay.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, support@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: High latency + 5xx wave on dedicated pool (ClearPay reserved capacity)

Olga / Redwood support team —

We're seeing a sustained latency increase and ~7-10% 5xx error rate from our reserved pool starting 08:45 PST. Token throughput is capped below our expected committed throughput and we're observing spikes in queueing depth; several production customers are reporting API timeouts.

I've attached a zip with request traces and a CSV summary of token/latency metrics. This is impacting payments authorizations (transactions failing) — operations are seeing retries in the wild. Can you confirm whether this is a ClearPay-side burst or a Redwood capacity constraint? We're in a renewal window and this level of impact is critical.

Please advise next steps — we need an ETA.

--
Thomas Li
Head of Engineering, ClearPay
thomas.li@clearpay.com
attachments: clearpay_errlog_20261123.zip, pool_metrics_11-23.csv

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: High latency + 5xx wave on dedicated pool (ClearPay reserved capacity)

Forwarding ClearPay's report — key points: sustained latency, 5xx wave, and reserved throughput below commit. Logs/metrics attached.

Immediate asks:
- David / Rishi: can you triage (root cause, quick mitigation) and confirm whether this is a Dedicated pool saturation / noisy neighbor / runtime regression?
- Marissa: please prepare a short customer update (what we know, actions, ETA) for Thomas and the ClearPay execs.
- Vivek: flagging for visibility—if we need short-term burst capacity or emergency prioritization, we may need exec signoff.

Timing: ClearPay needs an ETA within 30 minutes. If this is a capacity shortfall, we should prepare an authorization request for burst GPUs and credits (approx estimate in David/Rishi reply).

Notes: ClearPay is a top-tier reserved customer (DEAL-7632), highly sensitive to downtime during business hours.

--
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: High latency + 5xx wave on dedicated pool (ClearPay reserved capacity)

Acknowledged — we've pulled the ClearPay pool metrics. Early read: queue depth and mean latency jump correlate with a sudden increase in tail sequence lengths from a small set of tenants pinning the KV cache; token throughput per GPU is ~30% below baseline for the 08:40–09:20 window. 5xxs appear to be upstream timeouts from our runtime when requests exceed the per-device concurrent stream limit.

Immediate mitigation we can push in the next 10–20m:
- Apply temporary per-tenant concurrency throttle (limit tenant QPS to committed baseline) — should reduce queueing.
- Route high-latency requests to a hosted-compatible model variant (lower memory footprint) as a fallback for non-sensitive paths.
- Warm/prime KV cache for ClearPay's hot prefixes (manual cache preloading script attached).

If these fail or throughput gap remains >15%, we'll need to allocate burst GPUs to ClearPay's pool (estimated +8 A100-equivalent for 4 hours) and enable expedited provisioning. That requires exec approval and an emergency billing/credit carve-out (rough estimate: $12k).

I'll run the throttle + route change now and report back.

--
David Kim
Director, Customer Operations
david_kim@redwood.com
attachments: pool_metrics_11-23.csv, kv_cache_warm_script.sh

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: High latency + 5xx wave on dedicated pool (ClearPay reserved capacity)

Thanks — running through runbook steps now. Quick technical summary:
- Root cause hypothesis: sudden shift in request length distribution + aggressive beam-search sampling from a single tenant is overflowing the KV eviction policy and causing repeated recomputation; that, combined with a per-device CUDA stream saturation, produces downstream 5xx timeouts.

Planned immediate actions (in progress):
1) Engage tenant-level throttle (David) — in prod in 2–5m.
2) Enable model-variant fallback for non-critical endpoints (switch routing policy for ClearPay's non-auth flows).
3) Spin up preemptible GPU pool (8 x A100) in us-west-2, attach to ClearPay's reservation as temporary burst. Estimated time to attach: 22–35 minutes depending on provisioning.
4) Apply runtime kernel parameter tweak (reduce max concurrent streams per device) to minimize upstream 5xx risk — requires quick restart window (2m) on affected nodes.

Estimated recovery timeline: if throttle + fallback effective, partial relief within 10–25m; full throughput restoration with burst GPUs within ~45m.

Requesting immediate exec approval for the preemptible GPU allocation and emergency credit:
- Resource ask: 8 A100-equivalent for 4 hours (preemptible), region us-west-2.
- Cost estimate: ~$12,000 (we can credit ClearPay for half if they prefer).

Attached: abbreviated preemptive_burst runbook. I'll post logs and a short RCA doc once stabilized.

--
Rishi Malhotra
SRE Lead, Runtime
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
attachments: runbook_preemptive_burst.pdf

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Fwd: High latency + 5xx wave on dedicated pool (ClearPay reserved capacity) — Exec approval request

Vivek — tagging you for approval. Cleary the triage indicates a capacity/eviction pressure scenario; David and Rishi propose an emergency preemptible allocation (+8 A100-equivalent) to restore contract throughput while we apply long-term mitigations (KV policy tuning, per-tenant quotas, and model-variant guidance).

Decision needed:
- Approve immediate preemptible allocation for ClearPay (8 A100-eq for 4 hrs) and emergency credit of up to $12k (we propose Redwood covers 50% to preserve relationship).
- If approved, ops to mark this an "expedited provisioning" and accelerate the attach flow; Marissa will send a one-paragraph customer update once we're green.

Customer context: ClearPay is at-risk for renewal conversations next week (deal 7632). This outage is in their peak region (US PST business hours). Our options are: let the routing/throttle partially restore (slower) or spend to return to committed throughput quickly.

Please reply with approval or alternative instruction — if I don't hear back in 10 minutes I'll assume we should proceed with throttle+fallback only and escalate to CEO if we cannot stabilize in 30 minutes.

--
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
